entries.why: Content-Type values are produced per response by a running system; no JGates check inspects live responses.
Redirect behavior between schemes is defined by the deployed server or proxy configuration.

checks.covers: A model checks who can supply host and proxy metadata and whether trusted ingress strips client-sent copies.
checks.misses: The behavior of the real ingress layer, which source review cannot confirm; only the application code it reads.

entries.why: The audit class examines exactly whether a client can supply values that the application takes from its own intermediary.
Which methods are blocked is decided in the server or gateway configuration at runtime.
Whether message signing is required is a design decision recorded by people, and no JGates check looks for it.

checks.covers: A model reviews how components decide where one request ends, including length headers and downgrade paths.
checks.misses: Load balancers, firewalls and servers outside the repository; only configuration and code that is present.

entries.why: The audit class is the request-smuggling analysis the requirement is about, limited to what can be read in the source.
No check compares generated Content-Length values with the length of the content.

checks.covers: The block names forbidden connection-specific headers and the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 downgrade among the framing issues it reviews.
checks.misses: Handling inside intermediaries and servers that are not in the repository.

entries.why: The audit class includes connection-specific header handling across protocol versions, which is the subject of the requirement.

checks.covers: The block includes CR and LF conversion as a normalization difference between components.
checks.misses: Servers and proxies outside the repository decide whether such bytes are accepted.

entries.why: The audit class covers control characters in header handling between components, which bears on this requirement.
No check measures the length of outgoing URIs or header values.
No check looks for query depth, amount or cost limits.
No check reads GraphQL server settings for introspection.
No check looks for non-TLS WebSocket URLs.

checks.covers: A model checks whether the upgrade accepts ambient cookies from an untrusted origin without an Origin check or channel token.
checks.misses: Servers whose handshake code is not read, and deployed proxies that filter origins.

entries.why: The audit class examines the Origin check on the upgrade handshake, which the requirement asks for.
No check examines how WebSocket sessions are tokenized.
No check examines how a WebSocket token is obtained.
